newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's Karlovacka brewery positively bubbling.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's Karlovacka brewery positively bubbling.

text.p: Shares in Croatian brewery Karlovacka Pivovara pushed ahead in mid-morning trade on the Zagreb Stock Exchange, fetching 530 kuna compared to Friday's close of 500 kuna, traders said.
The rise reflected solid gains made last week when Karlovacka, majority-owned by Chilean Cervecerias Unidas, bubbled to 500 from 360 kuna only two weeks ago.
A package of 2,000 Karlovacka shares was sold at 520 kuna and another 100 shares at 530 kuna on Tuesday, said Josip Ivicic of Consult Invest brokerage.
Market participants linked its strong growth to a discrepancy between the share price which was viewed as low, and positive 1996 results.
Ivicic said there were still 70 times more buy than sell orders for Karlovacka, and predicted further growth. Traders said last week it could reach 600 kuna.
While Karlovacka was on the rise, electric manufacturer Koncar was heading downhill after a recent 30-percent jump.
The stock closed at 1,280 kuna on Friday, but the highest buying order on Tuesday -- the first working week day -- was put at 1,050 kuna with no shares traded.

Koncar's price rose after news that Deutsche Morgan Grenfell would help float its shares abroad, but the euphoria died down as investors realised it would not happen before the end of the year, Ivicic said.
